scit_lca.version_note: LCA v2 (strong perturbation + consistency loss); v1 retained as ablation reference but not used as official baseline

pcm.container: WAV (RIFF) for storage; raw PCM bitrate = 16000 * 16 = 256000 bps

encodec.note: Will resample 16kHz->24kHz for encoding, decode at 24kHz, resample back to 16kHz for evaluation

dac.note: DAC has a 16kHz model variant matching our sample rate exactly

opus.skipped_reason: ffmpeg/opusenc not installed on system; will be added in a follow-up exp4 run when traditional codec tools become available

codec2.skipped_reason: Optional baseline, not pursued in this run

audio_format.evaluation_format: All decoded audio resampled to 16 kHz mono before metric computation

payload_packet_schema.note: Conceptual schema for packetized payload accounting; actual payload is computed analytically (not transmitted) for fair comparison

metrics.ASR: skipped (no Whisper integration in this run)
metrics.RTF: computed for SCIT Base/LCA only; baseline RTF not measured (libraries vary in API style)

experiment_notes: Skip traditional codecs due to missing ffmpeg/opusenc. Comparison focuses on (a) SCIT-Speech low-load operating points (500/1000/1500 bps) versus (b) PCM upper bound and (c) two neural codecs (EnCodec, DAC) at multiple bitrates. Result must be honest: SCIT operates at 0.5-1.5 kbps which is BELOW most neural codec minimum bitrates; this is a different operating regime, not a head-to-head win.
